Hi Sam / Jordan —

Great call this morning — thanks for walking through your ingestion and assistant use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff: 

1) Success criteria (mutually agreed):
- Assist accuracy: intent match >= 85% on our pilot prompt set (measured by closed-loop evals).
- Latency: 95th percentile < 250ms for single-turn generation at your typical request size (~150 tokens).
- Cost: token cost <= target you shared (we'll model after first week of traffic).
- Integration: end-to-end demo with streaming responses and tool-calling by end of trial.

2) Evaluation plan / ownership:
- Acme: provide 300 prompt pairs for accuracy eval + production-like load tests (Jordan).
- Redwood: run baseline evals, provide weekly regression reports, and monitor latency/cost (Marissa / Monica).

3) Timeline (proposed):
- 10/7: Technical kickoff (30–45m) with Acme devs + Redwood SRE/SEs.
- 10/8–10/16: Integration window — SDK setup, streaming, and tool-calling tests.
- 10/19: First full-run eval and review.
- 10/23: Hand-off / extension decision meeting.

4) Integration plan highlights (top-level):
- Primary path: Redwood JS SDK + server-side API for streaming outputs.
- Alternatives: Direct REST calls to /v1/generate-stream for lightweight services.
- Tool calling: will use structured tool outputs + function-calling extension we discussed; sample contract attached.

5) Action items / next steps: 
- Acme: confirm dev attendees for 10/7 kickoff and share prompt set by 10/6 (Jordan).
- Redwood: send calendar invite for 10/7 and provide initial SDK snippets + checklist (Marissa).

I've attached a short POC checklist to help your team prepare (redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx). If this looks right I'll lock in the kickoff and loop in our solutions engineer for the technical session.

Thanks,

Hi Sam — quick technical follow-up to address the items Marissa captured and your questions: 

1) Streaming support:
- Redwood JS SDK exposes a "onToken" callback that yields partial tokens as they're generated; examples:
  const stream = client.generateStream({ model: "redwood-l1", prompt });
  stream.onToken(token => renderChunk(token));
  stream.onDone(() => finish());
- Works over standard HTTP(S); if you route through a corporate proxy the SDK supports fetch/axios adapters and you can stream via server-side proxy to avoid browser-level proxy issues.

2) Tool calling / webhooks:
- Yes — Redwood can POST to your internal webhook with a structured payload. We support HMAC-signed headers for authentication or a short-lived bearer token (you pick). Example payload: {"tool":"search","query":"...","context_id":"..."} and we expect a JSON response with a defined schema (sample schema attached).

3) Evaluation scripts / ownership:
- We'll provide a runnable eval harness (Python + Node) that you can run within your environment; alternatively we can run in our sandbox if you prefer to keep data offsite. The harness outputs a CSV with per-prompt metrics and a summary report. We'll share the repo link in the kickoff.

4) API routes & rate guidance (for planning):
- /v1/generate (sync) — simple request/response.
- /v1/generate-stream (streaming) — SSE/WebSocket-backed streaming.
- /v1/embeddings — batch embeddings for indexing.
- Rate note: default soft limit ~60 reqs/min per API key for stream endpoints; we can request bumps for POC traffic.

5) Telemetry & logging:
- We'll provide request IDs and trace IDs; you can configure retention and sampling for logs in the console.

I've attached a small text file with SDK snippets and the sample tool schema: sdk-integration-snippets.txt. I'm happy to join the kickoff to walk the devs through these examples.
